facts.text: Burbank got its name in 1869, after the town was incorporated the year before, to avoid confusion with another Ohio town called Bridgeport.
Burbank began as part of Canaan Township in the 1830s, where pioneers cleared forested land for farming and basic industry.
The railroad turned Burbank into a freight hub, letting farmers ship crops to larger markets and drawing new residents.
Burbank sits along Killbuck Creek, a winding waterway that helped early settlers irrigate their fields.
Dr. Emanuel Beekley Sr., who arrived in the 1840s, helped fight a smallpox outbreak and later built schools and churches in Burbank.
By the late 1800s Burbank boasted general stores, hotels, a blacksmith, and a high school, reflecting its growth.
